problemStatement.formal: For finite samples with nonnegative rational weights, Chebyshev and Paley-Zygmund style second-moment bounds control the size of large-value or positive-support sets.
problemStatement.plain: Records theorem-level metadata for the second moment method. The Lean files prove a finite Chebyshev inequality, qualitative and quantitative Paley-Zygmund bounds, and a second-moment existence estimate for nonnegative finite data.
whyMatters: Second-moment arguments are a standard probabilistic-method route from variance control to existence results.
The finite rational formulation gives reusable combinatorial estimates without needing measure-theory overhead.
The metadata exposes the exact theorem names needed to find the concentration and positive-support bounds.

proven: `chebyshev_finite` proves a finite Chebyshev inequality over a Finset with rational-valued data.
`second_moment_existence` proves a positive-support lower bound from a second-moment hypothesis.
`paley_zygmund_probability` records the quantitative Paley-Zygmund probability-form corollary.
The listed proof files are recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: General measure-theoretic probability-space versions and asymptotic random-graph applications are outside this finite metadata slice.
knownResults.goal: Backfill searchable metadata for the theorem-backed finite second-moment method files.
